title: Context-retention retrieval
description: A RETRIEVAL probe, not an intelligence probe. The model is shown an inventory of schema-shaped observation records carrying opaque sentinel ids and asked for one field of one record. A correct answer means it could find a token it was shown at a given depth in the prompt. Calling that `reasoning` would be the single easiest way to oversell a local model, so the field names here say retrieval and nothing else. The #230 overflow probe — filler text repeated until the server refused — is kept as a low-level control and is a different question: that one asks whether the server refuses cleanly, this one asks whether the context is USABLE.

sentinel_id.description: The sentinel asked for, echoed back. Opaque and unguessable by construction, so an echo is either retrieval or invention and never a lucky ordinal.

record_present.description: Whether that sentinel was in the inventory at all. Negative controls ask for a sentinel that was never placed; a model that answers `true` there has invented a record, which is a different failure from failing to find a real one.

requested_field.description: The field name asked for, echoed. Guards against a model returning the right record's wrong field and scoring as a hit.

field_value.description: The value read out. Empty is legitimate when record_present is false, and is scored as such rather than as a miss.

cited_record_ids.description: Which records it used. A retrieval that cites three records to answer about one is recorded, because it says something about how the answer was found.
